source.name: Arkansas Secretary of State, Official Results, 2024 General Election and Nonpartisan Judicial Runoff Election (GE2024_report.pdf)

ballot_text.source_title: Issue No. 1: A Constitutional Amendment to Provide that Lottery Proceeds May Be Used to Fund or Provide Scholarships and Grants to Arkansas Citizens Enrolled (the SOS report cuts the title short; the Governor's certification of 2024-11-21 prints it in full, 'in Vocational-Technical Schools and Technical Institutes'). Ours says only 'State Issue 1'.
ballot_text.type_quote: Issue No. 1: A Constitutional Amendment to Provide that Lottery Proceeds May Be Used to Fund or Provide Scholarships and Grants to Arkansas Citizens Enrolled

fact.quote: The amendment was proposed by H.J.R. 1006 during the 2023 Regular Session and adopted at the 2024 general election
fact.why: Proposed by the General Assembly, not by petition. The SOS-hosted annotated Constitution says Amend. 103 'was proposed by H.J.R. 1006 during the 2023 Regular Session'. H.J.R. 1006 itself (arkleg.state.ar.us, 94th General Assembly, Regular Session 2023) opens 'BE IT RESOLVED BY THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF THE NINETY-FOURTH GENERAL ASSEMBLY ... AND BY THE SENATE' and its Section 3 gives the popular name that equals the Issue 1 title; the vote totals in the note (1,029,102 for, 119,527 against) equal those in the Governor's certification for Issue No. 1. It is an amendment (to Art. 19, Sec. 14(b)). The resolution's own base wording is 'if a majority of the electors voting thereon at the election adopt the amendment'. Caveat: the note is a publisher's note; the SOS's own 2024 notice for Issue 1 was not found on its live pages (they list 2026 issues).

source.name: Arkansas Secretary of State (publisher of the file): Election Laws of Arkansas and Constitution of the State of Arkansas of 1874, 2025 Edition, annotation 'Publisher's Notes' to Amend. 103 / Amend. 104 (the notes are the publisher's, inside the SOS-hosted file)

p.not_computed: Ark. Const. art. 19, §22: text reads 'majority of the electors voting at such election'; the base (ballots on the amendment, or all ballots at the election) is not stated here. Amendment 7 states the initiative rule differently (see next object): the threshold turns on more than the yes share of those voting on the question, and the model forecasts that share only

source.name: Arkansas Secretary of State, Official Results, 2024 General Election and Nonpartisan Judicial Runoff Election (GE2024_report.pdf)

ballot_text.source_title: Issue No. 2: An amendment requiring local voter approval in a countywide special election for certain new casino licenses and repealing authority to issue a casino (the SOS report cuts the title short; the Governor's certification prints '... casino license in Pope County, Arkansas.'). Ours says only 'State Issue 2'.
ballot_text.type_quote: Issue No. 2: An amendment requiring local voter approval in a countywide special election for certain new casino licenses and repealing authority to issue a casino

fact.quote: The amendment was proposed by initiated petition and adopted at the 2024 general election by a vote of 638,655 for and 505,772 against.
fact.why: Initiated by petition. The SOS-hosted annotated Constitution says of Amend. 104 (which amended Amend. 100, Sec. 4, on casino licenses) that it 'was proposed by initiated petition and adopted at the 2024 general election by a vote of 638,655 for and 505,772 against'; those totals equal the totals the Governor's certification gives for Issue No. 2, and the Issue 2 title is about casino licenses. So it is an initiated constitutional amendment (not an act and not a General Assembly referral). Caveat: this is a publisher's note inside an SOS-hosted file, and the match to Issue 2 is by title and vote totals; the SOS's own 2024 per-issue notice (captioned by law 'CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT (OR ACT) PROPOSED BY PETITION OF THE PEOPLE', Ark. Code 7-9-116(c)) was not found on its live pages, which list 2026 issues.

source.name: Arkansas Secretary of State (publisher of the file): Election Laws of Arkansas and Constitution of the State of Arkansas of 1874, 2025 Edition, annotation 'Publisher's Notes' to Amend. 103 / Amend. 104 (the notes are the publisher's, inside the SOS-hosted file)

threshold.rule: majority of the votes cast upon the measure; expressly not required to be a majority of electors voting at the election
threshold.quote: Any measure submitted to the people as herein provided shall take effect and become a law when approved by a majority of the votes cast upon such measure, and not otherwise, and shall not be required to receive a majority of the electors voting at such election.
threshold.matched: by the type the ballot text states (amendment; data/measure/ballot-texts.json); the ballot text shows it is an amendment the people initiated (Amendment 7) [stated] (data/measure/ballot-texts.json)

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures
p.note: this route's back-test of statewide measures shows more near-even finishes than it forecast (12 against 9.1 within 1 point of ½, and 11 against 6.9 within 20,000 votes, 2018 to 2024), so p may be low
